clue.text: Caliph's comment about acquired skill

indicators.note: about suggests letters turned around and scattered, so the phrase before it is rearranged

parts.note: all fourteen letters of the two words, possessive S included

explanation.surface: A ruler's remark concerns some skill he has picked up.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is ignored: the S of Caliph's is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An accomplishment is a talent or ability gained through practice, such as playing piano or speaking French.

clue.text: Warning — pie is strangely sublime

indicators.note: strangely says the letters appear in an odd, unexpected arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cautionary note: this pie tastes oddly heavenly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sublime is so grand or beautiful that it fills the observer with awe and wonder.

clue.text: Desire secret right away

indicators.note: away tells us the item just named is sent off, removed from the word

parts.note: covert means hidden or secret
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A wish to keep something hidden immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: Take R out of COVERT to leave COVET.
explanation.definitionFit: To covet is to want something, especially another person's possessions, with strong longing; both work as verbs.

clue.text: Throw off scent of cider dispersed in vapour

indicators.note: dispersed means scattered about, so the word before it has its letters mixed
in places the jumbled letters inside the word that follows

parts.note: mist is fine water vapour in the air
the letters of cider rearranged

explanation.surface: A cider spilt in a fog hides a trail from tracking hounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw off scent' looks like part of the cider story, but it is the whole definition: to lead astray.
explanation.definitionFit: To misdirect is to send someone the wrong way, just as throwing pursuers off the scent leads them astray.

clue.text: Talk about going into passage for dish

indicators.note: going into puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a lane is a narrow passage or road

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the talk word is read from its end

parts.note: to gas is to talk idly at length

explanation.surface: Chatter heading into a corridor in search of something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: To gas is informal for chattering at length, which is why 'Talk' can stand for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is an Italian baked pasta dish layered with sauce and cheese, an example of a dish.

clue.text: Second method of fellow becoming braggart

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
the how of something is its method
taken as written
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A second way for a chap to turn into a boastful person.
explanation.definitionFit: A show-off is a person who boasts and displays abilities to attract admiration, just as a braggart does.

clue.text: Measure of time in lake

indicators.note: in puts the time symbol inside the lake word

parts.note: a mere is a lake or pond
T is the symbol for time

explanation.surface: Gauging how long something has spent in a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A metre is a unit of length, and also the rhythmic measure of poetry, so it is a kind of measure.

clue.text: Mice, say, in revolting study? It doesn't matter

indicators.note: in places the pests inside the study word
revolting here means turning over, so the study word is read upwards

parts.note: a den is a private study or workroom
mice are an example of vermin, signalled by say

explanation.surface: Mice in a disgusting room? Oh, never mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' poses as disgusting, which suits mice, but in a down clue it means turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying never mind dismisses something as unimportant, the same as remarking that it does not matter.

clue.text: Supernatural beings left during day before something's beginning

indicators.note: during puts the left letter within the span of the day word

parts.note: an eve is the day before a festival
L is the abbreviation for left

indicators.note: beginning picks only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of something

explanation.surface: Magical creatures departed the day before something began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Day before' is EVE, as in Christmas Eve; L goes inside it, then S follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Elves are small magical creatures of folklore, a type of being from beyond the natural world.

clue.text: Playful and caring but not happy

indicators.note: but not says one piece is to be excluded from the longer word

parts.note: supportive means caring and helpful
up means cheerful, in good spirits

explanation.surface: Someone frisky and kind, though not cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Sportive is a literary adjective for frolicsome or lively in a light-hearted, joking manner.

clue.text: Bury referee is at half way point

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body
to referee a dispute is to mediate in it

explanation.surface: A burial umpire is caught halfway through a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury looks like the Lancashire town, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Intermediate describes a position between two extremes or stages, lying in the middle.

clue.text: Bringing in mesh

definitions.meaning: first meaning: earning as clear profit
second meaning: fabric of knotted cord or wire

explanation.walkthrough: Bringing in sounds like hauling a catch in a mesh, but it means earning, as in netting a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both earning money as clear gain and a material made of interwoven strands with open gaps.

clue.text: Invade enclosure after some cricket

indicators.note: after says the enclosure word is placed second, following the cricket word

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket
a run is an enclosure for animals, like a chicken run

explanation.surface: Fans storm the ground after a bit of cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six deliveries; RUN is placed after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun a territory is to spread over and occupy it by force, as an attacking army does.

clue.text: Serves tea loudly in break

indicators.note: loudly says the word is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: someone serving tea pours it; in a non-rhotic British accent the word sounds the same as the answer

explanation.surface: Somebody dishes out tea noisily during a rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause is a short stop or interval in activity, the same as a break.

clue.text: Hated posh polar pun getting revised

indicators.note: revised means altered and rewritten, so the letters are reorganised

parts.note: U means upper-class
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A smart joke about the poles, reworked, is detested.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class or posh is a crossword staple; it joins the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpopular means disliked by many people, so a hated person or thing is unpopular.

clue.text: Moving five feet around circle at the start is productive

indicators.note: moving means shifting about, so these letters change places

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: at the start keeps only the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of circle

explanation.surface: Shuffling a few steps round a ring at the beginning gets results.
explanation.definitionFit: Something effective produces the intended result, so it is productive and successful.

clue.text: Returning second bobbins, sewers might replace these

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the abbreviation is written backwards

parts.note: sec is short for second
spools are reels or bobbins for thread

explanation.surface: Second-hand bobbins being brought back by people who sew.
explanation.walkthrough: Sewers reads as people who sew, given the bobbins, but means drains.
explanation.definitionFit: Cesspools are pits for collecting waste, an older system that modern drains and sewer pipes have superseded.

clue.text: Dependable agent united board

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative or agent
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football club names
a board is a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A reliable representative joined the company board.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputable means having a good reputation and so able to be trusted or relied upon.

clue.text: Implore leaders of scouting expedition to enter wood

indicators.note: to enter places those letters inside the tree word

parts.note: beech is a hardwood tree

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so only the first letter of each word is kept

parts.note: first letters of scouting and expedition

explanation.surface: Pleading with the heads of a scouting trip to go into the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: To beseech is to beg urgently or earnestly, which is to implore.

clue.text: Organ left by rear of vestry working before much time passes

parts.note: the ear is an organ of hearing
L is the abbreviation for left

indicators.note: rear of picks the last letter of the word that follows

parts.note: last letter of vestry
on means operating or working

explanation.surface: A church organ left at the back of the vestry, playing soon after.
explanation.walkthrough: Organ suggests the church instrument in the vestry, but it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Early on means at an initial stage, soon after the beginning, before a great deal of a period has elapsed.

clue.text: Bad place, bad moods

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters are spoiled and put in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An unpleasant spot breeds foul tempers.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'bad' plays two roles: the first is part of the definition, the second signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodom is the biblical city destroyed for its wickedness, a byword for a sinful or depraved place.

clue.text: Children replacing head of smoked fish with head of narwhal

indicators.note: replacing tells us one letter takes the place of another

parts.note: kippers are smoked herrings

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: first letter of narwhal

explanation.surface: Swapping the front of a kipper for a narwhal's head.
explanation.walkthrough: The K at the head of KIPPERS gives way to N; nippers is British slang for small children.
explanation.definitionFit: Nippers is an informal British word for young kids.

clue.text: Former lover with skill upset auxiliary

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the skill word in this down clue is turned upside down

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: An old flame with talent upset a helper.
explanation.definitionFit: An auxiliary is something additional or supplementary, and an extra is an added or spare item.

clue.text: Epitaph and finale containing note came to fruition

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is a common epitaph

indicators.note: containing means the finale word holds the note inside it

parts.note: the finale is the end
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A gravestone inscription and a closing piece with one note brought matters to completion.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit that has ripened is mature, so to have ripened is to have come to fruition in a figurative sense.

clue.text: Antelope found in colony alarmingly

indicators.note: found in says the letters are discovered tucked inside the following words

parts.note: the tail of colony runs into the start of alarmingly

explanation.surface: A grazing beast is spotted in a settlement, worryingly.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned southern African antelope, a particular species of that animal.

clue.text: Smoother youngster initially providing cajolement

parts.note: flatter means more smooth and level

indicators.note: initially keeps only the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of youngster

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking youth starts sweet-talking someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Smoother suggests a smooth talker, but it is the comparative adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Flattery is excessive praise used to win favour, which is what cajolement means.

clue.text: Koalas strangely left out somewhere in Japan

indicators.note: strangely says the remaining letters fall in an odd order
left out is read as the left abbreviation being omitted from the word

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Strange koalas are absent from a place in Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove L from KOALAS, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a major port city on Honshu, so it is one particular location in that country.

clue.text: Respite from rabidly preaching beast

indicators.note: rabidly suggests wild, frenzied disorder, so the letters are thrown into chaos

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rest from some monster sermonising furiously.
explanation.definitionFit: A breathing space is a short pause allowing recovery, which is what a respite offers.
